answer: The reef wardens plant coral fragments on the damaged reef, and each fragment is tagged with its own number and mapped to the square metre where it was set. A horizon fragment bought from a dealer fails the registry: at the mirror of the tag the coral must match the reef's own planting log, and bought coral grows on no mapped square. Faking a reef means hiring divers, planting two hundred fragments and paying 23,400, while the atlas entry in the registry is kept for ten years, so a fragment whose planting was never logged is pulled out.
